stages.title: 1. Foundations: global infrastructure & identity
stages.why: Every design answer starts with accounts, identity and encryption. Interviewers probe least privilege and multi-account setups early.
concepts: Encryption at rest and in transit

stages.title: 2. Networking
stages.why: Networking questions separate SAs from developers. Be able to draw a VPC across 2 AZs and explain hybrid connectivity.
concepts: Public vs private subnets, IGW, NAT

stages.title: 3. Compute
stages.why: Choosing between EC2, containers and serverless, and justifying the choice, comes up in almost every scenario.
concepts: Instance families and purchase options (On-Demand, Spot, Savings Plans)
ECS vs EKS; Fargate vs EC2 launch type

stages.title: 4. Storage
stages.why: Know which storage fits which access pattern, plus durability and cost trade-offs.

stages.title: 5. Databases
stages.why: "SQL or NoSQL, and why?" is a classic. Know HA, read scaling and caching for each engine.
concepts: Aurora storage architecture and Global Database
DynamoDB keys, GSIs, capacity modes, global tables

stages.title: 6. Integration & decoupling
stages.why: Loose coupling is the backbone of resilient, scalable designs. Expect "SQS vs SNS vs EventBridge vs Kinesis".
concepts: Queue vs pub/sub vs event bus vs stream

stages.title: 7. Operations, IaC & resilience
stages.why: SAs are judged on operability. Pair these with the Well-Architected pillars and DR strategies in Learn.

stages.title: 8. Generative AI
stages.why: AWS SA interviews now routinely include GenAI. Know RAG, guardrails and agents on Bedrock.
concepts: Model choice, cost and latency trade-offs

stages.title: 9. Level up: security, data, migration & cost
stages.why: Once the core feels solid, these make senior-level answers stand out.
